content: The response of insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) to growth hormone (GH) analogs may require higher doses of GH for efficacy. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can lead to significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, and close monitoring is advised. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, and coadministration should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Lumequine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. Ferrous fumarate reduces manganese levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitoring is recommended. Norethindrone acetate increases the levels of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use non-CYP450-affected contraceptive methods or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ferrous fumarate reduces methyl dopa levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitoring is recommended. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol decreases metyrapone effects through an unspecified mechanism. Discontinuation of estrogens, including oral contraceptives, may be advisable before and during metyrapone administration. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing serum concentrations and prolonging sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ferrous fumarate, norethindrone acetate, and ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitoring is recommended. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ferrous fumarate decreases minocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, and coadministration should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Dose adjustment of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. Monitoring is recommended. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ferrous fumarate decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using alternative or additional forms of contraception. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol increases the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Nizatidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. Ethinylestradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating these agents and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the hepatitis C combination drug regimen.
